stem: A client with stable chronic heart failure says, "I get tired when I try to finish all of my household tasks at once." Which teaching by the nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Divide household tasks into manageable periods, schedule rest between activities, and follow the individualized physical-activity plan from the health care team.
options.B: Complete the household tasks in one block while energy is highest, then use the remainder of the day for rest so activity does not need to be interrupted.
options.C: Avoid routine household activity whenever fatigue occurs and resume the usual workload only after several days without activity-related tiredness.
options.D: Continue each planned task until it is finished despite increasing fatigue, then rest before beginning the next task so the daily workload remains unchanged.

rationale: American Heart Association guidance supports regular physical activity that is individualized to the person's heart health and recommends scheduling daily rest and relaxation to avoid overdoing activity and ease tiredness. The client's problem is trying to complete all tasks at once, so dividing tasks and planning rest while following the individualized activity plan is the best teaching. B concentrates the workload rather than pacing it. C promotes unnecessary inactivity rather than an individualized activity plan. D deliberately continues through increasing fatigue instead of using planned rest to avoid overexertion.
educational_objective: Teach a stable client with heart failure to pace daily activity by dividing tasks into manageable periods, scheduling rest, and following an individualized physical-activity plan rather than concentrating activity or avoiding it unnecessarily.
source_document_title: Lifestyle Changes for Heart Failure; Develop a Physical Activity Plan for You
source_version_date: Current AHA heart-failure guidance accessed 2026-08-25; physical-activity resource last reviewed April 24, 2024
source_locator: Lifestyle Changes for Heart Failure > Be physically active: regular moderate-intensity physical activity is encouraged, and the amount/type should depend on heart health with an activity plan designed with the health care/cardiac rehabilitation team. > Get enough rest: schedule time every day for rest and relaxation; daytime rest can help prevent overdoing activity and ease tiredness. Develop a Physical Activity Plan for You > Watch for warning signs: stop activity and contact the health care professional for warning signs such as dizziness/lightheadedness, unusual or extreme shortness of breath, excessive fatigue, angina, or a fast/uneven heartbeat.
source_claim_supported: People with stable heart failure should use an individualized physical-activity plan and scheduled rest to avoid overdoing activity and reduce fatigue rather than avoiding activity or concentrating the entire workload into one period.

supporting_sources.document_title: Develop a Physical Activity Plan for You
supporting_sources.locator: Discuss type and amount of physical activity with the health care team; Watch for warning signs: angina, lightheadedness/dizziness/confusion, extreme fatigue, unusual or extreme shortness of breath, and fast or uneven heartbeat warrant stopping activity and contacting the health care professional.
supporting_sources.claim_supported: Physical activity should be individualized with the health care team and stopped for clinically important exertional warning signs.

blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort, printed pp. 35–37: implement measures to promote circulation including mobilization; Mobility/Immobility, printed p. 36: assess mobility, gait, strength and motor skills and evaluate responses to interventions; Rest and Sleep, printed p. 37: assess the client's sleep/rest pattern and intervene as needed and schedule care activities to promote adequate rest.
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — balancing activity and rest in chronic heart failure
correction_summary: Rebuilt all four teaching statements to remove the very long keyed answer and absolute-word cueing, narrowed the item to activity pacing and planned rest, and removed unnecessary symptom lists from the answer choices while retaining directly sourced safety context in the rationale.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Chronic heart failure — activity pacing and rest
audit_findings.stem: PASS — stable chronic heart-failure context identifies fatigue from clustering household tasks and asks one self-management teaching question.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS — directly combines individualized activity with planned rest, matching current AHA guidance; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — activity is appropriate, but concentrating the workload into one uninterrupted block conflicts with pacing and planned rest.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — reducing activity may be necessary during instability, but routine avoidance until fatigue-free is not the supported plan for a stable client.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — preserving activity is reasonable, but continuing through increasing fatigue conflicts with the purpose of planned rest to prevent overdoing activity.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — A is the only option that combines appropriate ongoing activity with planned rest and individualized guidance without adding a contradictory condition.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — B clusters effort, C promotes unnecessary inactivity, and D postpones rest despite increasing fatigue.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — option lengths are comparable and no keyed-only absolute wording remains.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Basic Care and Comfort explicitly includes mobilization and assessment/intervention for rest and sleep needs.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether completing work early or resting until fatigue resolves might be equally appropriate; AHA guidance explicitly supports individualized regular activity plus scheduled daily rest, leaving A uniquely best for this stable client.
